title: Vocabulary: working with others
keyIdea: Team words name the things good friends do together. Cooperate means working together on one job. Compromise means each friend gets some of what they want. Listen means look at the talker, wait, and say back what you heard. You can disagree kindly, with calm words. Include means asking others to join, so nobody is left out.

kid: A team is a group that works on one job. When we work together, we cooperate. Two friends can lift a big log that one friend cannot lift.

Some days friends want different things. Fox wants red. Owl wants blue. A compromise is a plan where each friend gets a part. They paint it half red and half blue. If only Fox gets his way, that is not a compromise.
To listen, look at the one who is talking. Wait until they stop. Then say back what you heard: "You want a bridge?" Now they know you heard them.
It is OK not to agree. Say it in a kind way: "I see it a different way." Do not say "Your idea is silly." And look out for friends on their own. Ask them to join in. That is how we include them.
adult: This lesson gives children the words for the habits that friendships and group work depend on. In England, the statutory Relationships Education guidance for primary schools asks pupils to learn about caring friendships and respectful relationships, including how to manage conflict and how to seek help. In the early years, the EYFS goal Building Relationships asks children to work and play cooperatively and take turns with others. The CASEL framework calls these relationship skills: listening well, cooperating, and resolving conflict constructively.

Key words for ages 5 to 8: team, cooperate, share, take turns, compromise, listen, active listening, agree, disagree respectfully, and include. Active listening means facing the speaker, not interrupting, and responding to what was actually said. A compromise means both sides give a little so that each gets part of what they wanted.

Common mistakes: thinking compromise means giving in, so the quieter child always loses out. Mixing up cooperate (working together on one job) with include (inviting someone in). Thinking that being quiet is the same as listening, even while playing with a toy. And thinking that disagreeing is always unkind, so children either stay silent or say "Your idea is silly."

In the lab your child drags Fox and Bear to lift a log neither can lift alone. They choose fair plans when Fox and Owl want different things, and tap the signs that show Bear is listening. They sort kind and unkind ways to disagree, and drag Duck and Mouse into the team so the tower grows. Every drag has a big button twin.

familyTip: Next time two of you want different things, such as which film to watch, say "Let's find a compromise" and plan it together, like half of each or one now and one next time. Afterwards, ask your child: "Did we both get some of what we wanted?"

visual.caption: Which team word fits? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: Two friends carry a heavy bag together
We all tidy the room so it is done fast
You pick the game today, I pick tomorrow
Half red and half blue, so we both like it
Giving the new child a job in the game

lab.caption: Flagship lab: lift a log together, find fair plans, spot real listening, sort kind ways to disagree, and include friends in the team.

practice.prompt: Fox and Owl paint a sign together. Fox paints one half and Owl paints the other half. Which word is that?
practice.hint: They are working on one job together. Which word means that?
practice.explain: They work together on one job, so they cooperate. Include would mean asking a new friend to join.

practice.prompt: {n} friends build a den. 1 friend is on her own, and they ask her to join. How many friends build the den now?
practice.hint: Start with the {n} friends. Asking her to join adds 1 more.
practice.explain: {n} and 1 more is {=n+1}. Asking her to join means they include her, so nobody is left out.

practice.prompt: Mia wants to play tag. Sam wants to play ball. Which plan is a compromise?
choices: Only tag, and Sam must agree
practice.hint: In a compromise, each friend gets some of what they want.
practice.explain: Tag first, then ball gives each friend a part. If only Mia gets her way, Sam just gives in.

practice.prompt: {n} friends take turns on the slide. Each friend has 1 turn, then the next friend goes. How many turns is that?
practice.hint: Count 1 turn for each of the {n} friends.
practice.explain: Each of the {n} friends has 1 turn, so that is {=n} turns. Taking turns is one way a team cooperates.

choices: Do the job all on your own
pool.hint: Think of Fox and Bear lifting the big log.
pool.explain: To cooperate is to work together on one job, like two friends lifting a log that one friend cannot lift.

choices: Each friend gets some of what they want
pool.hint: Think of the sign painted half red and half blue.
pool.explain: A compromise is a fair plan: each friend gives a little and gets a part of what they wanted.

pool.prompt: Owl is telling Bear an idea. Which shows Bear is listening?
choices: Bear looks at Owl and waits
pool.hint: Listening signs: look, wait, then say back what you heard.
pool.explain: Looking at Owl and waiting shows Bear is listening. Being quiet with a toy is not the same as listening.

pool.prompt: You do not like your friend's idea. Which is a kind way to disagree?
pool.hint: You can say what you think and still be kind.
pool.explain: "I see it a different way" tells your friend what you think, calmly. Calling an idea silly hurts.

pool.prompt: A new child stands on her own at play time. How can you include her?
choices: Ask her to join your game
Let her watch from far away
pool.hint: Include means asking someone in, so they are not left out.
pool.explain: Asking her to join includes her. Watching from far away still leaves her out.

pool.prompt: After Owl talks, Bear says, "You want to build a bridge?" Why does Bear say that?
choices: To show he heard Owl's idea
pool.hint: Saying back what you heard is a listening sign.
pool.explain: Saying it back shows Owl that Bear really heard the idea. It is part of active listening.

pool.prompt: {n} friends are in a team. 2 friends are on their own, so the team asks them to join. How many are in the team now?
pool.hint: Start at {n} and count on 2 more.
pool.explain: {n} and 2 more is {=n+2}. The team included the 2 friends, so nobody is left out.

pool.prompt: Fox wants to paint. Owl wants to build. Fox shouts until Owl gives up. Is that a compromise?
choices: No, only Fox got his way
pool.hint: Did each friend get some of what they wanted?
pool.explain: No. Owl gave in, so only Fox got his way. A compromise gives each friend a part, like paint first, then build.

pool.prompt: Fox and Owl make a compromise. They play Fox's game for {n} minutes, then Owl's game for {n} minutes. How many minutes do they play in all?
pool.hint: Add Fox's {n} minutes and Owl's {n} minutes.
pool.explain: {n} + {n} = {=2*n} minutes. Each friend got some of what they wanted, so it is a compromise.
